([[Beverly Hills, Michigan]]) | college = [[Xavier Musketeers men's basketball|Xavier]] (2014–2017) | draft_year = 2017 | draft_round = 2 | draft_pick = 52 | draft_team = [[New Orleans Pelicans]] | career_start = 2017 | years1 = {{nbay|2017|start}}–{{nbay|2020|end}} | team1 = [[Indiana Pacers]] | years2 = [[2017–18 NBA G League season|2017]]–[[2018–19 NBA G League season|2019]] | team2 = →[[Indiana Mad Ants|Fort Wayne Mad Ants]] | years3 = {{nbay|2022|full=y}} | team3 = [[Brooklyn Nets]] | years4 = 2023–2024 | team4 = [[BC Žalgiris|Žalgiris Kaunas]] | years5 = 2024–2025 | team5 = [[Sichuan Blue Whales]] | years6 = 2025–present | team6 = [[Guangdong Southern Tigers]] | highlights = * [[Chinese Basketball Association scoring leaders|CBA scoring champion]] ([[2024–25 Chinese Basketball Association season|2025]]) * [[Karaliaus Mindaugo taurė|Lithuanian King Mindaugas Cup]] winner ([[2023–24 King Mindaugas Cup|2024]]) * Second-team [[List of All-Big East Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big East]] (2016) }} '''Edmond Byron Sumner''' (born December 31, 1995) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Guangdong Southern Tigers]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]] (CBA). A [[point guard]], he played [[college basketball]] for the [[Xavier Musketeers men's basketball|Xavier Musketeers]] and averaged 15.0 points per game as a junior. ==College career== Sumner spent three years playing for the Xavier Musketeers (at [[Xavier University]], Cincinnati) from 2014 to 2017.{{Cite news|url=https://goxavier.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=2114|title=Edmond Sumner Profile-Men's Basketball-Xavier University|work=goxavier.com|access-date=February 17, 2019}} Sumner was sidelined with an injury in an 82–77 win against [[St. John's Red Storm men's basketball|St. John's]] in January 2017 and did not play the rest of the season. At that point, he was averaging 14.9 points, 4.9 assists and 4.4 rebounds per game.{{Cite news|url=http://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/xavier-might-have-lost-starting-point-guard-edmond-sumner-for-the-season/|title=Xavier might have lost starting point guard Edmond Sumner for the season|work=CBSSports.com|access-date=April 5, 2017}} This was not the first time he had suffered knee issues; his freshman season was cut to just six games as he withdrew from further playing due to chronic tendinitis in his knees.{{Cite news|url=https://eu.cincinnati.com/story/xaviersports/2014/12/16/edmond-sumner-headed-for-medical-redshirt/20478039/|title=Edmond Sumner sidelined by chronic tendinitis|work=cincinnati.com|access-date=February 17, 2019}} On March 28, 2017, Sumner declared for the [[2017 NBA draft]].{{Cite web |last=Brennan |first=Patrick |title=Xavier's Edmond Sumner announces he's entering NBA Draft |url=https://www.cincinnati.com/story/sports/college/xavier/2017/03/28/xaviers-edmond-sumner-announces-hes-entering-nba-draft/99734232/ |access-date=2024-09-25 |website=The Enquirer |language=en-US}} ==Professional career== ===Indiana Pacers (2017–2021)=== On June 23, 2017, Sumner was selected 52nd overall in the [[2017 NBA draft]] by the [[New Orleans Pelicans]], only to be traded to the [[Indiana Pacers]] in exchange for cash considerations.{{Cite web |last=Brennan |first=Pat |title=Edmond Sumner selected in NBA Draft, dealt to Indiana Pacers |url=https://www.cincinnati.com/story/sports/college/xavier/2017/06/23/edmond-sumner-selected-nba-draft-dealt-indiana-pacers/422322001/ |access-date=2024-09-25 |website=The Enquirer |language=en-US}} Sumner signed a [[two-way contract]] with the Pacers on July 5, 2017, becoming the first second round draft pick to sign such a deal. In the 2017–18 season, Sumner struggled for minutes and spent significant time with the Pacers' G-League team, the [[Fort Wayne Mad Ants]]. Sumner's limited minutes continued into the beginning of the 2018–19 season, but when teammate [[Victor Oladipo]] suffered a season-ending injury of a [[quadriceps tendon rupture]] his playing time increased significantly, and was given his first NBA start, against the [[Golden State Warriors]].{{Cite web|url=https://8points9seconds.com/2019/01/30/nba-edmond-sumner-indiana-pacers/|title=Breaking down Edmond Sumner's first NBA start with the Indiana Pacers|work=8 Points 9 Seconds|date=January 30, 2019 |access-date=February 17, 2019}} On February 11, 2019, Sumner signed a standard NBA contract with the Pacers,{{cite web|title=Pacers Sign Edmond Sumner|url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers-sign-edmond-sumner|date=February 11, 2019|website=NBA.com|access-date=February 11, 2019}} which was reported to be a two-year contract.{{cite web|title=Pacers Sign Edmond Sumner To Two-Year Contract|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/wiretap/252631/Pacers-Sign-Edmond-Sumner-To-Two-Year-Contract|date=February 11, 2019|website=realgm.com|access-date=February 11, 2019}} On July 29, Sumner inked a three-year contract worth $6.48 million with the Pacers after declining his $1.6 million team option in late June.{{Cite web|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/tonyeast/2019/08/30/edmond-sumners-new-contract-displays-the-indiana-pacers-belief-in-his-future/#720da06b745f|title = Edmond Sumner's New Contract Displays the Indiana Pacers' Belief in His Future| website=[[Forbes]] }} During the 2020–21 season, Sumner averaged 7.5 points and 1.8 rebounds per game, shooting 52.5 percent from the floor. In April 2021, he posted consecutive 20-point games against the [[Detroit Pistons]] and the [[Orlando Magic]].{{cite news |last1=Glaspie |first1=Akeem |title=Pacers guard Edmond Sumner out indefinitely with torn left Achilles |url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/nba/pacers/2021/09/09/pacers-guard-edmond-sumner-suffered-torn-left-achilles/8263114002/ |access-date=September 10, 2021 |work=[[Indianapolis Star]] |date=September 9, 2021}} On September 9, 2021, it was announced that Sumner would be sidelined indefinitely with a torn Achilles tendon.{{cite news |last1=Feldman |first1=Dan |title=Pacers: Edmond Sumner tore his Achilles |url=https://nba.nbcsports.com/2021/09/09/pacers-edmond-sumner-tore-his-achilles/ |access-date=September 10, 2021 |work=[[NBC Sports]] |date=September 9, 2021}} === Brooklyn Nets (2022–2023) === On October 6, 2021, Sumner was traded, alongside a 2025 second-round pick, to the [[Brooklyn Nets]] in exchange for the draft rights to [[Juan Pablo Vaulet]].{{cite web|title=Brooklyn Nets Complete Trade With Indiana Pacers|url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/2021/10/06/brooklyn-nets-complete-trade-indiana-pacers|website=NBA.com|date=October 6, 2021|access-date=October 6, 2021}} Four days later, he was waived by the Nets.{{cite web|title=Brooklyn Nets Waive Edmond Sumner|url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/2021/10/10/brooklyn-nets-waive-edmond-sumner|website=NBA.com|date=October 10, 2021|access-date=October 10, 2021}} On July 8, 2022, Sumner re-signed with the Nets.{{cite web|title=BROOKLYN NETS SIGN EDMOND SUMNER|url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/2022/07/08/brooklyn-nets-sign-edmond-sumner|website=NBA.com|date=July 8, 2022|access-date=July 9, 2022}} On July 15, 2023, Sumner was waived by the Nets.{{cite web|title=Brooklyn Nets Waive Edmond Sumner|url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/brooklyn-nets-waive-edmondsumner|website=NBA.com|date=July 15, 2023|access-date=July 15, 2023}} On September 29, 2023, Sumner signed with the [[Charlotte Hornets]],{{cite web|title=Hornets Sign R.J. Hunter And Edmond Sumner|url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/news/hornets-sign-r-j-hunter-and-edmond-sumner|website=NBA.com|date=September 29, 2023|access-date=September 29, 2023}} but was waived on October 24.{{cite web|title=Charlotte Hornets Sign Ish Smith|url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/news/charlotte-hornets-sign-ish-smith-2|website=NBA.com|date=October 24, 2023|access-date=October 29, [[EuroLeague]].{{cite web|title=Edmond Sumner officially signs with August 23, 2024, Sumner signed with [[Sichuan Blue Whales]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]] (CBA).{{cite web|title=Blue Whales land Edmond Sumner, ex Zalgiris|url=https://www.asia-basket.com/China/news/888574/Blue-Whales-land-Edmond-Sumner-ex-Zalgiris|website=Eurobasket|date=August 23, 2024|access-date=April 13, 2025}} He led the CBA in scoring in
